6 the authors and editors seem to be negotiating with this pre-existing archaic mythological story but then
later in the fourth third centuries BCE we get another renegotiation where uh Greco-Roman period authors are
negotiating with Genesis and expanding and elaborating on the very sparse story within Genesis and they create this more
elaborate mythological world now within the Book of Enoch the Nephilim are more implicitly The Offspring of these Fallen
Angels who are equated with the children of god mentioned in Genesis 6. and the Nephilim themselves have children who
are a separately named group as well now this gets discussed in the Book of Giants and other Dead Sea scroll texts
as well as in some early Christian literature but as with what's going on in Genesis what's going on in the enochic literature and the later
derivative literature is a renegotiation so in the end to answer the question of who the Nephilim are we first have to
determine which literary layer we're going to be examining because a picture emerges from what's going on in Genesis
a different picture emerges if you also bring the numbers layer into the discussion a different picture emerges if we look at the anarchic literature
and a still different picture emerges when we look at the derivative and the later renegotiations with the anarchic
literature so each literary layer is renegotiating between the layer that came before and the rhetorical goals and
the exigencies of whatever circumstances that are compelling them to write so there is no one single unified picture
